doc.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018

title: Worst gig: Leonard's of Great Neck wedding bands
summary: She was told to answer to 'Susie' as a stand-in singer, and decided she had to stop doing weddings.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: For the Obamas. So I’m in a picture with the Obamas with the band. So that was a big highlight. And you know, there are a lot of highlights. I mean Steely Dan, I love working with them. I love, you know, the first time, we’ve done Rochester Jazz Festival with my band several times. And the first time that people waited on-line to come to a gig of mine, that was like a highlight, I thought people are here, we don’t play for two hours. Really? So that was kind of, just the realization that people were actually coming to hear me was — . I’d say one of the worst — so there are a lot of bests you know. I’m fortunate. You know I shared the stage with Jimmy Heath a few years ago for the NEA Jazz Masters, and Poncho Sanchez on percussion and I mean it was like a great band. And it was like how do I get to stand on stage and sing with Jimmy Heath? That was amazing. And so I would say one of the worst was I used to do, when I was doing weddings, and there’s a place called Leonard’s of Great Neck and musicians will know about this. And so I was working for a wedding office that was booking me. And they had two bands. There’s an upstairs and a downstairs room. So we’re in the upstairs room and there’s another band in the downstairs room. And the vocalist for that band couldn’t make the gig for some reason. So they said to me, “Okay so you’ll sing upstairs and then when you take a break upstairs you’ll go downstairs and sing with this band. And then if they call you Susie you just say yes.” Because all they wanted was a black singer. They don’t care who it is. They just want somebody to sing whatever it was you know. So that was, I would have to say, okay, at that point I thought I don’t care how much money I don’t have I’ve got a find a way not to do this anymore. I just can’t do it anymore. Because I was doing them, three a weekend for twelve years or something like that. Friday, two on Saturday, one again, three or four a weekend. So I just though, you know, and it was paying my bills.
They would pair you with a band and you were supposed to know a certain repertoire?
